_comment: Which long-distance trails should wear a through-route badge, and what blaze their chip takes (#1543). map/trailBadges.ts draws one badge per through-route in view and takes its mark from BADGE_MARK_BY_SOURCE, which has two entries - the A.T. and the Long Path. Every other source falls through to the blaze chip in the trail's own hue. This file is the list that tier grows to.
_marks_live_in_org_marks: WHETHER A TRAIL'S MARK MAY SHIP IS NOT TRACKED HERE. sources.json's `org_marks` block records it per organization and pipeline/tests/test_org_marks.py enforces it, both of which predate this file. An earlier draft carried a per-trail `mark_state` mirroring that vocabulary; it was 67 rows all saying the same thing and tracking nothing org_marks did not already track, so it is gone. One record, in one place.
_why_this_exists: features/TRAIL_BLAZE_COLORS.md records that line WIDTH carries the hue-independent channel - a through-route is drawn wider than the spurs off it - and says outright that this 'answers it for exactly as long as that stays true', because 'a second through-route on the map turns the question width answers into through-route or spur'. The 11 new endpoints in features/ORG_BULK_LOAD.md are that second through-route arriving, several times over. An emblem is what answers WHICH through-route once width can only say THAT it is one.
_blaze_note: `blaze` is the trail's painted blaze where it has one and 'none' where it is signed rather than blazed. features/TRAIL_BLAZE_COLORS.md's rule is that a blaze colour in a map or a table is data, not decoration - which is why the chip can carry it and a mark cannot be invented to sit beside it.
_this_is_a_floor_not_a_census: 67 TRAILS IS WHAT ONE PASS FOUND, NOT WHAT EXISTS. Four regional audits on 2026-09-29 found 153 MORE long-distance trails at 40 miles or over, each with a named steward, and they did not finish - five states were never swept and the 1,358 National Recreation Trails were not enumerated at all. pipeline/reference/trail_candidates.json is that list, with the evidence grade each audit gave it and the public-domain federal service that would enumerate the rest. Nothing downstream breaks on the gap: a trail with no row here still draws as a named line, it just gets no badge. Read a missing trail as 'nobody has added it yet', never as 'it did not qualify'. Before adding any of them, read that file's four findings - there is no built-fraction field yet, and 17 of the 153 share treadway with a trail already listed here.
